decisions_log.chose: Allan primary, Fano alongside; broken-stick knee by exhaustive search compared to a single line by BIC
decisions_log.why: Allan tolerates a slowly varying rate, which is exactly the envelope being separated out. A spline or derivative-based knee finder would introduce its own bandwidth -- the class of free parameter D8 bars from the gate. Exhaustive search is deterministic and the BIC comparison TESTS a knee rather than assuming one.
With 20 rungs, BIC alone can prefer a two-segment fit whose bend is negligible. Requiring a real bend as well stops a statistically-supported non-knee from passing.

options_considered: derived from the T1 knee per event
decisions_log.chose: k_env = expected prints in a knee-duration window at the event's own mean rate
decisions_log.why: D8 requires the scale come from the gate, not from a sweep. Converting the knee to a per-event k keeps the estimator adaptive while making the scale non-free.

decisions_log.decision: gate rows scored on configured segments only
decisions_log.why: The first run also scored a `no_detection` stratum -- the 2 never-crossing events, which have no detection anchor and therefore no segment -- whose n=2 knee IQR of 1.957 decades failed row 7. Row 7's observable is defined 'within a segment'. This is a population error, not a finding. No threshold was moved; their curves are retained.

decisions_log.decision: chart 07 selection trimmed to the cap
decisions_log.why: The first selection was 64 against a cap of 60 and the script refused to write. dev_v4_primary is kept whole per the selection rule; the stratified draw is trimmed on an even index spacing over (segment, sub-burst count), so it still spans the count range within each segment. The pre-registered cap is a constraint, not a target to adjust.

surprises: Row 0 fired again. This is the second consecutive phase version in which every numeric criterion that mattered behaved -- including the Arm A test that v1 failed and v3 passed -- while Cooper's visual review against the tape rejected the result. Producing chart 07 despite the numeric failures is the only reason that judgment was available; v2 skipped its equivalent and could not be judged at all.

The scale-separation gate PASSES, and cleanly: dBIC 45.6-68.7 with slope changes 0.61-0.87 on all four segment-by-observable cells. After four failed methods, a characteristic clustering scale does exist.

The Allan factor never approaches the Poisson value 1 anywhere on the ladder -- rth/print median is 5.99 at 15.6 ms and 1245 at 4096 s. Clustering is present at EVERY scale measured; the knee marks where the rate of increase changes (slope 0.173 -> 1.017), not where clustering starts. Easy to misread off log-log axes, and I did misread it once before checking the numbers.

Row 1 -- the Arm A test -- PASSES for the first time in this phase. Spearman 0.277/0.353 and log-log slope 0.261/0.185 against Arm A's 0.96 and 0.85. The envelope-relative reference appears to remove the mechanism that made Arm A's burst count a restatement of print count.

Row 3 fails badly and is the substantive result: sub-burst sets computed at the two ENDS of the knee's own bootstrap interval overlap by a median Jaccard of 0.0735 (print) / 0.1071 (volume). The gate certifies that a scale exists; row 3 says the knee is not sharp enough to pin the decomposition it licenses.

Premarket and regular-hours differ by ~8x in knee (16s vs 128s) and ~6x in sub-burst count (median 131 vs 20). D8(d) made segment a stratification variable from the start; this is the strongest evidence yet that it had to be.
The two observables disagree more than expected -- Spearman 0.4233 on sub-burst count, and levels differ 27 vs 70. Print rate and share-volume rate are not measuring the same object here.

Session activity duration spans only ~0.35 decades across the cohort against ~3 decades for print count, so the +1.425 duration slope in the row-1 diagnostic is fitted over a far narrower range than the print-count slope and carries less weight than its size suggests.
